// why: Node 23.6+ runs .ts directly by stripping types — no build step, no dist/, no
chance of the shipped JS drifting from the source. The price is that only
erasable syntax is allowed: no enums, no namespaces, no parameter properties.
erasableSyntaxOnly makes tsc enforce that, so a construct that would crash at
runtime fails typecheck instead of failing in front of a user.
Everything else here is strictness. The point of the conversion was to make
mistakes visible, so the checks that catch real defects — unchecked indexing,
optional properties treated as present, unused values — are all on.
